response: Yes, loss of consciousness can predict neuropsychological decrements after concussion. Research has shown that individuals who experience a loss of consciousness (LOC) after a concussion are more likely to exhibit cognitive and neuropsychological impairments, such as memory problems, attention deficits, and decreased processing speed, compared to those who do not lose consciousness. The duration and severity of LOC can also be related to the severity of subsequent neuropsychological decrements.
